title: Jazz Limited, Sidney Bechet, and school work suffering
summary: He frequented Jazz Limited, preferred Dodds to Bechet, and his schoolwork suffered so he left after a year.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: I used to go there quite a lot because I knew people who were working there like Don Yule and Dick Wells did. I used to like to hear Sidney Bechet who was working there for a while.
Did you at any time show a tendency to follow Bechet or were you strictly on a Dodds game?

No, actually I didn't really like Bechet that much. I liked Dodds much better. And I went through a period later where I thought Bechet was terrible and absolutely unlistenable. And now I sort of come back to him. I like a good deal of his work. I think he's a great musician. You told me that you took lessons after you arrived in Chicago, right? No, I never took any lessons while I was in Chicago. How did you get along with school work and your interest in music? Did they match up? No, I'm afraid the school work suffered. That's why I only stayed there a year. And I never finished college. I was still possessed by this dream of becoming a jazz musician. And I think I had some illusions in those days that what I was doing was more important than it really was. In those days, I used to think that if you could play the same notes that Johnny Dodds did and if you played the same tunes, that you were doing the same thing. And of course it's not that easy.
